title: A particle whose velocity is given by a graph

plot.label: Graph of the velocity v(t) in meters per second for t from 0 to 12 seconds, made of segments through (0, 4), (2, 4), (6, -4), (8, -4), (10, 0) and (12, 2)

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A particle moves along the $x$-axis with velocity $v(t)$ shown in the graph, for $0 \le t \le 12$ seconds. Find the acceleration of the particle at $t = 5$. Is the particle speeding up or slowing down at $t = 5$? Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.point: $a(5) = v'(5) = -2$ meters per second per second (the slope of the segment from $(2, 4)$ to $(6, -4)$).
Speeding up, because $v(5) = -2 < 0$ and $a(5) = -2 < 0$ have the same sign.
accept: speeding up: velocity and acceleration are both negative at t = 5

parts.sample: $a(5) = v'(5) = \frac{-4 - 4}{6 - 2} = -2$ m/s². Since $v(5) = -2 < 0$ and $a(5) < 0$, velocity and acceleration have the same sign, so the particle is speeding up.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: At what times $t$ in $0 < t < 12$ does the particle change direction? Justify your answer.

rubric.point: Justification: $v$ changes sign at each time (positive to negative at $t = 4$, negative to positive at $t = 10$).
accept: v changes sign at t = 4 and at t = 10

parts.sample: $v(t)$ changes from positive to negative at $t = 4$ and from negative to positive at $t = 10$, so the particle changes direction at $t = 4$ and $t = 10$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The particle is at $x = 5$ at time $t = 0$. Find its position at $t = 12$.

accept: x(0) plus the integral of v from 0 to 12

parts.sample: $\int_0^{12} v(t)\,dt = 8 + 4 - 4 - 8 - 4 + 2 = -2$ (a rectangle, two triangles on $[2, 6]$, a rectangle, a triangle below the axis, a triangle above). So $x(12) = 5 + (-2) = 3$ meters.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the total distance the particle travels over $0 \le t \le 12$. At what time is the particle farthest to the left? Justify your answer.

accept: positions at the endpoints and at the direction changes

rubric.point: Farthest left at $t = 10$, where $x(10) = 1$ is the least of the candidates.
accept: t = 10 with x = 1 and a candidates comparison

parts.sample: Total distance $= \int_0^{12} |v(t)|\,dt = 8 + 4 + 4 + 8 + 4 + 2 = 30$ meters. The particle can be farthest left only at an endpoint or where $v$ changes sign: $x(0) = 5$, $x(4) = 5 + 12 = 17$, $x(10) = 17 - 16 = 1$, $x(12) = 1 + 2 = 3$. The least is $x(10) = 1$, so it is farthest left at $t = 10$.
